name: MonarchUsageMeter
title: UsageMeter
summary: Usage against limits: for each metered item, what was used, the limit and a meter that turns to the warning color near the limit and the danger color over it, with the level written as text.
whenToUse: On a billing or plan screen, to show quotas of requests, storage, seats or minutes for the current period.
whenNotToUse: For the progress of a task use MonarchProgress. For one reading against bands use MonarchGauge. The meter only shows usage; upgrading or buying more goes through the app's own flow and the store's billing rules.
api: @Composable fun MonarchUsageMeter(items: List<MonarchUsageMeterItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, period: String? = null, resetsAtMillis: Long? = null, warningAt: Double = 0.8, loading: Boolean = false, announceChanges: Boolean = false, error: String? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchUsageMeterLabels = MonarchUsageMeterLabels(), announceThresholds: Boolean = false)
class MonarchUsageMeterItem(label: String, used: Double, limit: Double? = null, unit: String? = null, description: String? = null, id: String = label)

class MonarchUsageMeterLabels(amount: ((used: String, limit: String) -> String)? = null, percent: ((percent: String) -> String)? = null, nearLimit: String? = null, overLimit: String? = null, resets: ((date: String) -> String)? = null, loading: String? = null, retry: String? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The metered items, in display order. An item without a limit shows the count alone.

options.name: period
options.description: The period measured, such as "This month".

options.name: resetsAtMillis
options.description: When the quota resets, in epoch milliseconds (UTC). Written as a medium date in the current locale and the device time zone.

options.name: warningAt
options.description: The share of the limit at which an item is near the limit.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a progress indicator and "Loading usage" instead of the items.

options.name: announceChanges
options.description: Makes every item a polite live region, so TalkBack announces an item whose figures or level change while it is on screen.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message shown instead of the items. It wins over loading.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a "Try again" MonarchButton under the error.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces any of the built-in strings (monarch_usagemeter_*).

options.name: announceThresholds
options.description: Announces once, for the whole meter, the items that have just reached the warning share or gone over their limit ("Storage: Near the limit"), through one polite live region. Nothing is read when the meter first appears.

states.name: normal
states.description: The meter is filled in the accent color and the line under it reads "42% used".

states.name: near the limit
states.description: At or above warningAt: the warning color and "Near the limit · 84% used" in warning text.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: Above the limit: a full meter in the danger color and "Over the limit · 130% used" in danger text.

states.name: unlimited
states.description: No limit, or a limit of zero or less: the count and the unit, with no meter.

states.name: loading
states.description: A circular progress indicator and the loading text replace the items.

states.name: error
states.description: The message in danger text replaces the items, with a retry button when onRetry is given.

appearance: The meter uses the accent solid, warning solid or danger solid color on the emphasis background track. The status line is muted text, or warning strong and danger strong text near and over the limit; the error message is danger strong. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchProgress for each item; MonarchProgress has no color or tone parameter, so the meter uses the Material 3 LinearProgressIndicator directly with the level colors. The web lays items out in a grid or a list; on a phone they are one column, as on iOS, so there is no layout option. The web loading state draws skeleton tiles and the error state uses InlineErrorRetry; here loading is a progress indicator with text and the error is a message with a Monarch button. The web shows a warning or error icon next to the level; Monarch bundles no icons, so the level is written as text in the level color. The web announces level changes by default; on Android a component that is on screen from the start makes announcements opt-in, so announceChanges is off by default. The reset date is epoch milliseconds, as in the Material 3 DatePickerState. The eight built-in strings are replaced through MonarchUsageMeterLabels, as on iOS.
accessibility: Each item is one TalkBack element that reads its label, its figures and its status line, for example "Storage, 42 of 50 GB, Near the limit · 84% used". The meter itself is hidden.
Near and over the limit are written as text, so they do not depend on the color of the meter.
With announceChanges every item is a polite live region.
The error message is a polite live region, and the retry button is a Monarch button with a 48dp touch target.
The loading indicator and its text are read as one element.
All text scales with the font size and wraps; it is not cut off at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Used above the limit draws a full meter; the percentage shows the real share, such as 130%.
Exactly at the limit is near the limit, not over it.
A limit of zero, a negative limit or a limit that is not finite is treated as no limit.
The error takes precedence over loading.
The unit is written after the figures with a space, in every locale.
Numbers are written with at most one fraction digit in the current locale.

MonarchUsageMeter(

    title = "Usage",
